name: Question 6
problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨8{t}^{3},-1⟩.
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨-1,\,3⟩$ when $t=1,$ calculate the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t=3.$
worked_solution:
To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨8{t}^{3},-1⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 8{t}^{3}\,\text{d}t,\,\int -1\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨2{t}^{4}+{C}_{1},\,-t+{C}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(1)=⟨-1,3⟩.$ Substituting $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨2(1)^{4}+{C}_{1},\,-(1)+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨-1,3⟩ & =⟨2+{C}_{1},\,-1+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=-3$ and ${C}_{2}=4.$ Therefore, the velocity is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =⟨2{t}^{4}-3,\,-t+4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity at time $t=3$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =⟨2(3)^{4}-3,\,-(3)+4⟩ \\  & =⟨159,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

The acceleration a at time t of a particle P moving in the xy-plane is given by a(t)=⟨8t3,−1⟩. Given that the particle has velocity v=⟨−1,3⟩ when t=1, calculate the velocity vector of P at time t=3.

a
v(3)=⟨−3,4⟩
b
v(3)=⟨159,1⟩
c
v(3)=⟨6,−3⟩
d
v(3)=⟨162,1⟩
e
v(3)=⟨162,−3⟩
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector: v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫⟨8t3,−1⟩dt=⟨∫8t3dt,∫−1dt⟩=⟨2t4+C1,−t+C2⟩.

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that v(1)=⟨−1,3⟩. Substituting t=1, we get

v(1)=⟨2(1)4+C1,−(1)+C2⟩⟨−1,3⟩=⟨2+C1,−1+C2⟩,

so we must have C1=−3 and C2=4. Therefore, the velocity is given by

v(t)=⟨2t4−3,−t+4⟩.

Finally, the velocity at time t=3 is

v(3)=⟨2(3)4−3,−(3)+4⟩=⟨159,1⟩.
